Consumers should call seamClauseOne_of_isGaloisQuotient_noMatch.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, and it is the whole of what remains: k'-side representability itself. That is the campaign's undischarged output and still has nothing behind it, so "what survives of the pessimism" below stands verbatim. Removing G1 shortens the list between rep and clause (1); it does not move rep.

--- earlier node text follows ---

ROUTE CORRECTION 2026-07-29 (review-ajc): THE CAMPAIGN'S DESCENT STEP TARGETS A FALSE STATEMENT.
Read this before choosing a target under this node. Corrected twice the same day; this is the
settled version.

THE FACT, now a Lean theorem reduced to one named residue. ajc-p1's
PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso (Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean:427) proves
that if picEtComparison C fails to be an isomorphism then NO scheme represents picSharp C -- the
EXISTENTIAL of clause (1), not a pinned candidate -- with no topology and no sheaf step in the
argument. Axiom-clean. Kleiman supplies the curve, L5105-L5108 (repeated L5126-L5129) in
references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex: the conic u^2+v^2+w^2=0 in P^2_R, a smooth plane
conic and hence SMOOTH, PROPER, GEOMETRICALLY INTEGRAL over a field where it has NO rational point
-- exactly this project's binders -- with Pic_{(X/R)et} representable by s4 th:main and the two
functors differing (ex:Pfs). So UNCONDITIONAL representability of picSharp over an arbitrary field
is FALSE, not merely open. THE ONE UNFORMALISED STEP, stated so nobody reads this as closed: that
the comparison really does fail for that conic (via phi^*O(1) and h0 on P^1_C).

THE CONSEQUENCE. The campaign's last two milestones claim exactly that: G3 concludes "J_r :=
J'_r/Gamma represents picSharpDeg C r OVER k" and G4 assembles picSharpDeg. Those two AS WRITTEN
aim at a false statement. Corrected in informal/pic-representability-campaign.md at G3.

DO NOT REBUILD THIS VIA A ZARISKI-SHEAF ARGUMENT -- two citations have already been wrong in that
slot (I-0970, I-0973, and the lesson is worth more than the fact):
 * the seam's original "picSharp is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman s2 L1292-L1302)" cites lines
   about the ABSOLUTE functor Pic_X. The relative functor quotients by Pic(T) precisely to defeat
   that argument. That bad citation had propagated to four Lean docstrings, the campaign and the
   blueprint; all corrected (2b7e53f2d, 0aad6b59b).
 * my own replacement, ex:Pfs, is wrong in the SAME slot for a different reason: it compares the
   two SHEAFIFICATIONS zar and et, both already sheaves, so it witnesses zar != et and says
   nothing about Zariski descent for the unsheafified picSharp. Withdrawn in 3a7a58a02.
 * th:cmp part 1 (L1391-L1393) points the other way: Pic_{X/S} INJECTS into Pic_{(X/S)zar}
   whenever O_S = f_*O_X universally, automatic here -- so picSharp is Zariski-SEPARATED on these
   binders. Consistent with campaign B1, whose audit note says its sheaf statement is false only
   WITHOUT the section.
 * ajc-p1's Lean theorem picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy is TRUE, axiom-clean and
   worth keeping. It just does not supply half of this refutation.

WHAT SURVIVES -- nearly everything, so this is not a reason to stand down. The obstruction is
absent over a SEPARABLY CLOSED field, where a section is cheap, and that is where P1-P5, B0-B6,
D1'-D4', J1-J5 and G2 all run. Every item currently claimed under this node is BELOW the break:
ajc-p1's D2' (divgrassmannian), ajc-p3's D3' (divlocallyclosed), ajc-p4's B5 (semicontinuity).
The break is exactly where the field returns to k: G1/G3, and G4 downstream.

THE REPAIR, needing no specification change. The object that descends to k must be picEt, not
picSharp. Over k' the two agree (section => Kleiman 2.5, or ajc-p1's
isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf from representability over k'), so J5's output IS a
picEt-representing scheme after base change. Restating G3 to descend picEt points -- carried by
the sheaf property picEt HAS and picSharp lacks -- reaches clause (1) of fgaPicardRepresentability
with no false intermediate. This is what makes AJC.picrep.etale-rep priceable rather than
unpriced, and it is a rewrite of the campaign's last two milestones rather than a new obligation.

--- PREVIOUS SUMMARY, still accurate on the landed/absent split ---

REOPENED active by review-ajc 2026-07-29 (was `done`, which was wrong in the strongest available sense: the deliverable this node advertised does not exist).

THE ONE OPEN OBLIGATION, named. `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` in `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (de-lined 2026-07-30, review-ajc r7: this said `:377` with `theorem head :369`, and at HEAD the head is 757 and the sorry 765 — 377 lands mid-docstring, the very defect this row's own NOTE ON THE CONSUMER INTERFACE forbids. Four AJC rows had reproduced it at 347/371/377; all de-lined. Do NOT refresh these into numbers) — a BARE `sorry`. Statement: for a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over an ARBITRARY field `k`, (1) the etale-sheafified relative Picard functor `PicScheme.picEt C` is representable by a `k`-scheme that is `LocallyOfFiniteType` and `IsSeparated`, AND (2) `HasRationalPoint C -> IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)` (Kleiman section 2 Thm 2.5). Everything else on the seam is a projection of it.

WHY THE OLD `done` WAS FALSE, verified three ways this round. (a) The advertised deliverable `instHasPicScheme` exists in NO `.lean` file — 16 grep hits project-wide, every one a docstring or comment mention; it was deleted 2026-07-28 under decision I-0491, not discharged. (b) `AJC.picrep.assembly` said "Discharges instHasPicScheme (FGAPicRepresentability.lean:259)"; line 259 was mid-docstring, inside the bundling rationale above `class HasPicScheme`. Corrected on that node. (c) A `done` parent over the open child `AJC.picrep.tensor` had been warning for some time.

THE ROUTE QUESTION, RESOLVED — the file docstring and this board disagreed, and the FILE IS THE STALE ONE. `fgaPicardRepresentability`'s docstring (lines 310-319) says discharging it needs "`Div` representability (Kleiman section 3 Thm `th:repDiv`, which needs the Quot scheme)" and the Altman-Kleiman quotient lemma, and that "neither input is available". Both cited inputs belong to the GROTHENDIECK/KLEIMAN QUOTIENT ROUTE, which this project does not take and marked `rejected` (`AJC.picrep.quot`, `AJC.picrep.serre`). The committed route is MILNE-KOLLAR (D3, `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`), whose Cluster D' reaches `Div^d` representability through the GRASSMANNIAN — D1' fibre-degree slices, D2' the Grassmannian embedding, D3' locally-closed carving, D4' `Div^d` as a scheme with a quasi-projectivity CERTIFICATE (a locally closed immersion `Z_d -> Gr`) — and never through Quot. The quotient step is likewise not `smoothProperQuotient`: it is G2, the FINITE GALOIS quotient of a semilinear action whose finite orbits lie in affine opens, which is landed (`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`, 550 lines, sorry-free). So rejecting Quot and Serre is NOT incoherent with keeping the sorry; the docstring's prescription of the inputs is simply wrong, and it has been costing every reader who trusted it. Issue filed; the docstring is corrected in place.

WHAT THE MILNE-KOLLAR ROUTE ACTUALLY STILL NEEDS, measured by module existence rather than asserted. LANDED: B0 `Picard/SectionRingUniversal.lean`, B2 `Picard/FinitePresentationFunctor.lean`, B3 `Picard/RigidPushforward.lean` + the discharged gate `AJC.picrep.rigidpushforward`, D1'/A2 `Picard/DivDegree.lean`, G2 `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean` + `GaloisDescent/`, P2 `RiemannRoch/CohomologyKit.lean`, and the whole Grassmannian/flattening/graded substrate (`AJC.grquot`, sorry-free, with `Grassmannian.representable` proved). ABSENT AS MODULES, i.e. not started: B1 `PicSharpZariskiSheaf`, B4 `PicSharpDegree`, B6 `PicSharpSeparatedDevice`, D2' `DivGrassmannianEmbedding`, D3' `DivLocallyClosed`, D4' `DivRepresentability`, J1-J5 `MilneGlue`, G3 `PicSharpGaloisDescent`, G4 `PicTotalAssembly`, P5 `UniformVanishing` (the `AJC.rr.extuniform` leaf, open). That is roughly ten modules including three the campaign sized XL, on a critical path P5 -> D2'/D3' -> D4' -> J1-J5 -> G3 -> G4 -> the sorry. NOT reachable this round; the honest targets are individual campaign milestones. CLAIM LEDGER, RE-READ AT HEAD 2026-07-30 (review-ajc r5): the four claims this row used to name --
D2' by ajc-p1, D3' by ajc-p3, B5 by ajc-p4, P5 by ajc-p2 -- are ALL STALE. Every one of those rows
has an EMPTY owner at HEAD, the lanes having released or repointed. So `AJC.picrep.divgrassmannian`,
`AJC.picrep.divlocallyclosed`, `AJC.picrep.semicontinuity` and `AJC.rr.extuniform` are UNCLAIMED and
available. The only AJC rows owned by a live lane at the time of writing are
`AJC.picrep.sepclosed-finite` (ajc-p3) and `AJC.pic0av.properness` (ajc-p4). Do not read THIS ROW for
who holds what -- read `roadmap list --json` and filter on owner. A claim ledger copied into prose
goes stale within the hour; this paragraph is kept only to say so.

THE ELEVENTH ITEM IS WITHDRAWN -- IT WAS REFUTED IN-TREE, AND BY THE TIME I RE-READ IT THE REFUTATION HAD BEEN SITTING IN THE PROJECT FOR HOURS (review-ajc, third pass, 2026-07-29; kernel-verified).

WHAT TWO EARLIER PASSES OF THIS SAME LANE PUBLISHED HERE, as the round's headline finding: "every campaign milestone targets picSharp while clause (1) is about picEt; the gap CANNOT be closed by composing with picEtComparison, which is an iso only under a section -- so completing all ten modules leaves the sorry open." The middle clause is false, and it is the one the conclusion rests on.

THE REFUTATION, in this project, axiom-clean. `Scheme.picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` and `Scheme.hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability` (`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean:263`, `:286`) prove that a scheme representing `picSharp C` represents `picEt C` -- SAME scheme, so LocallyOfFiniteType and IsSeparated ride along unchanged -- with NO hypothesis on `C(k)`. `Scheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability` (`:310`) gives clause (2) unconditionally, strictly stronger than the seam's own section-gated conjunct. `#print axioms` on all three: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. No sorryAx. Probed in a scratch file under AlgebraicJacobian/, `lake env lean` EXIT=0, file deleted.

WHY THE ARGUMENT FAILED, since the mechanism is the reusable part. "picEtComparison is an iso only under a section" is Kleiman 2.5's hypothesis, and I treated a sufficient condition as the only one. Representability supplies the SAME sheaf property that the section was buying: a representable presheaf is a sheaf for a subcanonical topology (`relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy`, from `subcanonical_etaleTopology`), and a sheaf's sheafification unit is an iso (`isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf`). So at the campaign's own endpoint the section is redundant -- the hypothesis I-0491 forbids was never needed for the transport.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE FOUR LANES. The ten campaign modules ARE the right target after all: their picSharp-shaped output transports to clause (1) for free. There is no eleventh module. AJC.picrep.etale-rep is a route repair at G1/G3 (descend picEt rather than picSharp across the FIELD change), not a missing representability theorem -- ajc-p1 landed exactly this and released it (I-0976). Do NOT re-derive the transport, and do NOT plan an eleventh module.

WHAT SURVIVES OF THE PESSIMISM, so this is not read as the seam being close. Both antecedents above are the campaign's UNDISCHARGED output: the transport CONSUMES picSharp representability and does not produce it. Ten modules including three XL remain absent as modules, on the critical path P5 -> D2'/D3' -> D4' -> J1-J5 -> G1/G3 -> G4. Still not reachable this round. And the G3-level refutation is untouched and is the real obstruction: UNCONDITIONAL representability of picSharp over an arbitrary field is FALSE (see the ROUTE CORRECTION block at the top of this row), so the descent step must carry picEt points across the field change. The correction here is that this is ONE repair at the descent step, not a repair plus an unscheduled eleventh module.

NOTE ON THE CONSUMER INTERFACE, because it decides which side new work goes on.

correcting FOUR stale line numbers. Eight hours later ALL of its anchors were stale again, by 45 to

/bin/bash -lc "
python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from archon_horizon.search.index import extract_declarations
import re
root=Path(\"MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge\")
rows=[]
for p in root.rglob(\"*.lean\"):
    try: txt=p.read_text()
    except: continue
    for d in extract_declarations(txt, library=\"AJC\", file=str(p)):
        if \"RepresentableBy\" in d.signature:
            rows.append((str(p),d))
print(\"DECLS\",len(rows))
for p,d in rows:
    sig=\" \".join(d.signature.split())
    print(f\"{p}:{d.line}:{d.name}\\n  {sig}\")
PY
"

- blueprint — Own one assigned blueprint slice end-to-end — keep it pure math with complete proofs, cite references with \source{...} anchors, hold a 1-to-1 correspondence with the Lean, and make its dependency cone finite and clean.
- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.
- janitor — Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done).
- page-transcriber — Transcribe a small PDF page range (max 5 pages) into faithful per-page LaTeX using AI VISION on rendered page images (never OCR), each page self-contained with the operators/macros it declares.
- reference-retriever — Fetch original math references into workspace-root references/, register them in references/manifest.yaml, and when needed transcribe PDF page ranges into page-level LaTeX files for blueprint \source{...} anchors.
- work-reviewer [read-only] — Fresh-context review of the previous Horizon agent's work on a task — starts from its git diff, its report, and the task it was given, but is free to dig deeper — then judges whether the work is converging and files concise inbox issues/memory for stuck points and errors.
- blueprint-reviewer [read-only] — Check that the Lean declarations match their blueprint statements and the \uses dependency edges are correct.
- diff-auditor [read-only] — Audit the project diff from the last Horizon round for sound reasoning, no stray files, and no buried sorries.

Delegate by spawning a subagent **by name** through your engine's own subagent mechanism, giving it a focused directive: the slice/scope and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Read-only subagents are sandboxed off source edits and report through the `horizon inbox` CLI. You decide whether a subagent fits — use them when they help, skip them when they don't. Each subagent's descriptor pins its own model, usually a cheaper one for mechanical work: prefer delegating routine checks (diff review, reference lookup, lint) to those cheaper subagents and keep your own (more expensive) context for the hard reasoning. - Run the project build after Lean/blueprint edits so generated Lean artifacts and

  `.archon-horizon/blueprints/<project>.json` for the dashboard and cached DAG

- Use `horizon leandag` for live inspection when deciding what to prove next.

## `horizon leandag` (preferred)

- `horizon leandag` — per-project summary: nodes, edges, proved count, and any
  isolated nodes (no edge in or out — usually a blueprint bug to fix).
- `horizon leandag -p <project> --node <label>` — one node's direct deps, full
  transitive cone, and reverse deps.
- `horizon leandag -p a -p b --union` — merge projects by declaration/node id.
  Same-id nodes are combined; divergent non-signature metadata is tolerated, but
  a Lean signature mismatch is an error to investigate.
- `horizon leandag -p a -p b --intersect` — only shared declaration/node ids,
  with the same signature check.
- Add `--json` for machine-readable output.

choosing what to attempt next.

## Cached JSON

`horizon blueprint` writes each project's DAG to
`.archon-horizon/blueprints/<project>.json` (`nodes`, `edges`, `dangling`) for
the dashboard. Under the leandag engine, `\uses` are resolved at build/cache
time, so `dangling` is empty there; the parser fallback still populates it. To
check for orphan/unresolved nodes, use `horizon leandag` rather than relying only
on `dangling`.

`proved`/`leanok` status, effort metrics, and Lean source metadata.

## Keep It Fresh

- Run the project build after Lean/blueprint edits so generated Lean artifacts and
  imported libraries are current.
- Run `horizon blueprint` after blueprint or Lean declaration changes; it writes
  `.archon-horizon/blueprints/<project>.json` for the dashboard and cached DAG
  consumers.
- Use `horizon leandag` for live inspection when deciding what to prove next.

## `horizon leandag` (preferred)

- `horizon leandag` — per-project summary: nodes, edges, proved count, and any
  isolated nodes (no edge in or out — usually a blueprint bug to fix).
- `horizon leandag -p <project> --node <label>` — one node's direct deps, full
  transitive cone, and reverse deps.
- `horizon leandag -p a -p b --union` — merge projects by declaration/node id.
  Same-id nodes are combined; divergent non-signature metadata is tolerated, but
  a Lean signature mismatch is an error to investigate.
- `horizon leandag -p a -p b --intersect` — only shared declaration/node ids,
  with the same signature check.
- Add `--json` for machine-readable output.

A node is "ready" when all dependencies are proved. Prefer ready nodes when
choosing what to attempt next.

`horizon blueprint` writes each project's DAG to
`.archon-horizon/blueprints/<project>.json` (`nodes`, `edges`, `dangling`) for
the dashboard. Under the leandag engine, `\uses` are resolved at build/cache
time, so `dangling` is empty there; the parser fallback still populates it. To
check for orphan/unresolved nodes, use `horizon leandag` rather than relying only
on `dangling`.

# Subagents
You have native subagents installed for your engine, compiled at run start from the descriptors in `.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` (Claude reads `.claude/agents/`, Codex reads `.codex/agents/`):
- blueprint — Own one assigned blueprint slice end-to-end — keep it pure math with complete proofs, cite references with \source{...} anchors, keep each node faithfully aligned with the Lean it names, and make its dependency cone finite and clean.
- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.
- janitor — Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done).
- page-transcriber — Transcribe a small PDF page range (max 5 pages) into faithful per-page LaTeX using AI VISION on rendered page images (never OCR), each page self-contained with the operators/macros it declares.
- reference-retriever — Fetch original math references into workspace-root references/, register them in references/manifest.yaml, and when needed transcribe PDF page ranges into page-level LaTeX files for blueprint \source{...} anchors.
- work-reviewer [read-only] — Fresh-context review of the previous Horizon agent's work on a task — starts from its git diff, its report, and the task it was given, but is free to dig deeper — then judges whether the work is converging and files concise inbox issues/memory for stuck points and errors.

Delegate by spawning a subagent **by name** through your engine's own subagent mechanism, giving it a focused directive: the slice/scope and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Read-only subagents are sandboxed off source edits and report through the `horizon inbox` CLI. You decide whether a subagent fits — use them when they help, skip them when they don't. To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under `.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run.

YOU own the model choice for every piece of delegated work — a subagent spawned by name, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or a Workflow/orchestration if your engine offers one (including any automatic fan-out your session mode does for you). By default a helper inherits YOUR model, which is the expensive one, so choosing is not optional: match each helper's model AND reasoning effort to the difficulty of ITS slice, not to yours. Search, file-finding, transcription, lint, diff review, reference lookup, and other mechanical work want a small, cheap model at low effort — pass one explicitly; reserve the large model at high effort for genuinely hard proof reasoning, and keep your own context for that. Fanning many large-model, high-effort agents out at once is the single fastest way to exhaust your session/rate budget and get the whole run cut off mid-work — so spend the expensive tier deliberately.

# Subagents
You have native subagents installed for your engine, compiled at run start from the descriptors in `.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` (Claude reads `.claude/agents/`, Codex reads `.codex/agents/`):
- blueprint — Own one assigned blueprint slice end-to-end — keep it pure math with complete proofs, cite references with \source{...} anchors, keep each node faithfully aligned with the Lean it names, and make its dependency cone finite and clean.
- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.
- janitor — Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done).
- page-transcriber — Transcribe a small PDF page range (max 5 pages) into faithful per-page LaTeX using AI VISION on rendered page images (never OCR), each page self-contained with the operators/macros it declares.
- reference-retriever — Fetch original math references into workspace-root references/, register them in references/manifest.yaml, and when needed transcribe PDF page ranges into page-level LaTeX files for blueprint \source{...} anchors.
- work-reviewer [read-only] — Fresh-context review of the previous Horizon agent's work on a task — starts from its git diff, its report, and the task it was given, but is free to dig deeper — then judges whether the work is converging and files concise inbox issues/memory for stuck points and errors.

Delegate by spawning a subagent **by name** through your engine's own subagent mechanism, giving it a focused directive: the slice/scope and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Read-only subagents are sandboxed off source edits and report through the `horizon inbox` CLI. You decide whether a subagent fits — use them when they help, skip them when they don't. To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under `.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run.

YOU own the model choice for every piece of delegated work — a subagent spawned by name, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or a Workflow/orchestration if your engine offers one (including any automatic fan-out your session mode does for you). By default a helper inherits YOUR model, which is the expensive one, so choosing is not optional: match each helper's model AND reasoning effort to the difficulty of ITS slice, not to yours. Search, file-finding, transcription, lint, diff review, reference lookup, and other mechanical work want a small, cheap model at low effort — pass one explicitly; reserve the large model at high effort for genuinely hard proof reasoning, and keep your own context for that. Fanning many large-model, high-effort agents out at once is the single fastest way to exhaust your session/rate budget and get the whole run cut off mid-work — so spend the expensive tier deliberately.

     9	/-!
    10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
    11	
    12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
    13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
    14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
    15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
    16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
    17	
    18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
    19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
    21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
    22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
    23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
    25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
    27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
    28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
    29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
    30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
    31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
    32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
    33	-/
    34	
    35	set_option autoImplicit false
    36	
    37	universe u
    38	
    39	open CategoryTheory
    40	
    41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    42	
    43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    45	
    46	noncomputable section
    47	
    48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
    49	
    50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
    51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
    52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
    53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
    54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
    56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    57	
    58	section DegAt
    59	
    60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    61	
    62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
    63	@[simp]
    64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
    65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
    66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
    67	
    68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
    69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
    71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
    72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
    74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
    75	
    76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
    77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
    79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
    80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
    81	  rfl
    82	
    83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
    84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
    85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
    86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
    87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
    89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
    90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
    91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
    92	
    93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
    94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
    95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
    97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
    98	
    99	end DegAt
   100	
   101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
   102	
   103	variable (C) in
   104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
   105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
   106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
   107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
   108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   109	    degAt lam t = 0}
   110	  one_mem' := by
   111	    intro K _ _ t
   112	    exact degAt_one t
   113	  mul_mem' := by
   114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
   115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
   116	  inv_mem' := by
   117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
   118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
   119	
   120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
   121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
   122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
   123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
   125	  Iff.rfl
   126	
   127	variable (C) in
   128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
   129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
   130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
   131	points. -/
   132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
   133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
   134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
   135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
   136	
   137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
   138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
   139	@[simp]
   140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
   141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
   142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
   143	  rfl
   144	
   145	variable (C) in
   146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
   147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
   148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
   149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
   150	functor. -/
   151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
   152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
   153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
   154	  map_id T := by
   155	    ext lam U
   156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
   157	  map_comp g h := by
   158	    ext lam U
   159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
   160	
   161	@[simp]
   162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
   163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
   164	  rfl
   165	
   166	@[simp]
   167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
   168	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
   169	    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
   170	  rfl
   171	
   172	variable (C) in
   173	/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
   174	Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
   175	(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/", "parent_tool_use_id": "toolu_bdrk_01XCYXENFtJdVaZdRSLrp5Rn", "subagent_type": "general-purpose"}, "usage": null}

     6	import Mathlib
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicFunctor
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
    11	
    12	This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
    13	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
    14	for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
    15	central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
    16	
    17	## Why the sheafification is the right object
    18	
    19	The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
    20	(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
    21	a sheaf**, not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302): a line
    22	bundle on `C ×_k T` can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T` without
    23	being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`, because the gluing data is a `Pic`-class
    24	of the overlaps. Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
    25	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
    26	statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
    27	hypothesis.
    28	
    29	There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
    30	supplied:
    31	
    32	1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
    33	   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
    34	   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
    35	   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
    36	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
    37	2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
    38	   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
    39	   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).
    40	
    41	## The site
    42	
    43	Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
    44	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
    45	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
    46	lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
    47	transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
    48	`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
    49	corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
    50	"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
    51	and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
    52	hypothesis.
    53	
    54	## Main definitions
    55	
    56	* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
    57	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
    58	  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
    59	  relative Picard presheaf.
    60	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
    61	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    62	    Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
    63	  (CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj
    64	    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
    65	
    66	/-- **The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, as a standalone statement.**
    67	
    68	The underlying presheaf of `PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` satisfies the sheaf axiom
    69	for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled
    70	object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
    71	representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
    72	represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
    73	subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
    74	exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).
    75	
    76	Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/
    77	theorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    78	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    79	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
    80	  (etaleSheaf C).property
    81	
    82	/-- **The comparison map** `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, i.e. the unit of the
    83	sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.
    84	
    85	Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
    86	`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
    87	arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
    88	which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/
    89	noncomputable def toEtaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    90	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    91	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
    92	  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
    93	
    94	/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:
    95	every morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf
    96	of) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.
    97	
    98	This is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one
    99	sheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the
   100	sheaf into a universal receiver of relative Picard classes. -/
   101	noncomputable def etaleSheafHomEquiv {k : Type u} [Field k]
   102	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   103	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   104	    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
   105	    (etaleSheaf C ⟶ G) ≃ (PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ G.obj) :=
   106	  ((CategoryTheory.sheafificationAdjunction (etaleTopologyOver k)
   107	    AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).homEquiv (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) G)
   108	
   109	end PicSharp
   110	
   111	namespace PicScheme
   112	
   113	/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/
   114	
   115	/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:
   116	the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure
   117	forgotten,
   118	
   119	```
   120	picEt C : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1),   T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T).
   121	```
   122	
   123	Representability is a statement about the underlying set-valued functor; the
   124	group structure is transported back onto the representing scheme by Yoneda
   125	(`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), exactly as for the unsheafified
   126	`picSharp`.
   127	
   128	Contrast with `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget`: that functor is
   129	representable only under a rational-point hypothesis (it is not even a
   130	Zariski sheaf otherwise), whereas *this* one is the object of Kleiman §4
   131	Thm. `th:main` and its representability needs no hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/
   132	noncomputable def picEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   133	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
   134	    (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
   135	  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}
   136	
   137	/-- The comparison `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` of set-valued functors, the
   138	set-level shadow of `PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf`. An isomorphism under a
   139	`k`-rational point (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5), a comparison in general.
   140	
   141	The source is written out as `PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _` rather than as
   142	`picSharp C`, which is the *same functor by definition* but is declared in the
   143	downstream `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (that file imports this one, so
   144	the name is not available here). -/
   145	noncomputable def picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]

    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
    12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
    13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
    14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.

    20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
    21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
    22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
    23	
    24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
    25	
    26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
    27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
    28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
    29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
    30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
    31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.

    33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:

    36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
    37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;

    44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`

    34	that is what this file's obligation is stated against —

    36	hypothesis on `C(k)`**. The functor is built and its sheaf property proved in

    42	`picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is not representable over a
    43	general field — it is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2 L1292–L1302), and a

    25	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that

    27	hypothesis.

    36	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;

    11	
    12	`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds the Abel chart map `abelSigmaChart` out of a
    13	representation of the divisor functor, and its header states — correctly — that
    14	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
    15	scheme**: the Abel map has projective spaces `|D|` as fibres, so it is not even a
    16	monomorphism.  It becomes an open immersion only after restriction to the locus where the
    17	fibre is a single point.
    18	
    19	This file supplies the restriction, which is the half of C9b that needs no new mathematics
    20	once `chartLocus` exists — and it makes precise which half does.
    21	
    22	## What C9b consists of, and which part is here
    23	
    24	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) consumes a pair
    25	`(f, hf)`.  Producing it from `abelSigmaChart` factors into exactly two steps:
    26	
    27	1. **restrict the source along an open immersion** — `restrictChart` below.  Given any open
    28	   `V ⊆ D.left`, precomposing `abelSigmaChart` with `yoneda.map V.ι` gives a chart map out of
    29	   `V`, and this is a *composition* of presheaf morphisms.  Landed here, sorry-free.
    30	2. **certify the restricted map an open immersion of presheaves** — the honest content.
    31	   `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` (mathlib `MorphismProperty.relative`) has two clauses:
    32	   relative representability, and the open-immersion property of every represented pullback.
    33	   Step 1 supplies the *left* factor of both clauses for free
    34	   (`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map_of_isOpenImmersion` +
    35	   `MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`), so what remains is exactly the
    36	   corresponding statement for `abelSigmaChart` restricted to `V = chartLocus`, i.e.
    37	   CHART-U(c): on the chart locus the Abel map is a bijection onto its image because the
    38	   normalized effective representative is unique there (DAT-C GAP-2).
    39	
    40	So: the *composition* half of the `hf` certificate is discharged here, unconditionally; the
    41	*chart-locus* half is CHART-U(c) and is stated but not proved (it needs GAP-2 plus the
    42	classifier, and the openness of the locus itself, `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`).
    43	
    44	## CORRECTION 2026-07-29: step 2 above is itself TWO clauses, not one
    45	
    46	The description of step 2 as "*the* honest content" is right that it is not bookkeeping and
    47	wrong that it is a single obligation.  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` conjoins **relative

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeZero

     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
    11	
    12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
    13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
    14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
    15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
    16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
    17	
    18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
    19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
    21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
    22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
    23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
    25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
    27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
    28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
    29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
    30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
    31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
    32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
    33	-/
    34	
    35	set_option autoImplicit false
    36	
    37	universe u
    38	
    39	open CategoryTheory
    40	
    41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    42	
    43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    45	
    46	noncomputable section
    47	
    48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
    49	
    50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
    51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
    52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
    53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
    54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
    56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    57	
    58	section DegAt
    59	
    60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    61	
    62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
    63	@[simp]
    64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
    65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
    66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
    67	
    68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
    69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
    71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
    72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
    74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
    75	
    76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
    77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
    79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
    80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
    81	  rfl
    82	
    83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
    84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
    85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
    86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
    87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
    89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
    90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
    91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
    92	
    93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
    94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
    95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
    97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
    98	
    99	end DegAt
   100	
   101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
   102	
   103	variable (C) in
   104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
   105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
   106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
   107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
   108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   109	    degAt lam t = 0}
   110	  one_mem' := by
   111	    intro K _ _ t
   112	    exact degAt_one t
   113	  mul_mem' := by
   114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
   115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
   116	  inv_mem' := by
   117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
   118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
   119	
   120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
   121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
   122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
   123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
   125	  Iff.rfl
   126	
   127	variable (C) in
   128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
   129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
   130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
   131	points. -/
   132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
   133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
   134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
   135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
   136	
   137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
   138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
   139	@[simp]
   140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
   141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
   142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
   143	  rfl
   144	
   145	variable (C) in
   146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
   147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
   148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
   149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
   150	functor. -/
   151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
   152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
   153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
   154	  map_id T := by
   155	    ext lam U
   156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
   157	  map_comp g h := by
   158	    ext lam U
   159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
   160	
   161	@[simp]
   162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
   163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
   164	  rfl
   165	
   166	@[simp]
   167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
   168	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
   169	    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
   170	  rfl
   171	
   172	variable (C) in
   173	/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
   174	Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
   175	(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/", "parent_tool_use_id": "toolu_bdrk_01XCYXENFtJdVaZdRSLrp5Rn", "subagent_type": "general-purpose"}, "usage": null}

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianData
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0SigmaSheaf
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Producing the Jacobian representability datum from a Zariski chart family
    11	
    12	The pinned datum `JacobianData C` of the curve `C` bundles a representing object for the
    13	degree-zero Picard functor together with the two finiteness certificates of that object.
    14	This file constructs it: first from a bare representation (`JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy`),
    15	and then — the substance — from a Zariski chart family of the Σ-extension sheaf, whose glued
    16	scheme is the representing object and whose charts carry the finiteness.
    17	
    18	## Main declarations
    19	
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` — a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C`
    21	  by `J`, plus `LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom` and `QuasiCompact J.hom`, is a `JacobianData C`.
    22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedHom` / `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedOfCharts` — the glued scheme of a chart
    23	  family, placed over the base field by the Σ-component of the universal element of the
    24	  representation it induces.
    25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom` — the structure morphism `X i ⟶ Spec k` of the `i`-th chart:
    26	  the Σ-component of the element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.toGlued_comp_gluedHom` — **the compatibility of the two**: the glue map
    28	  `X i ⟶ gluedOfCharts` composed with the structure morphism of the glued object is exactly
    29	  `chartHom i`.  So the charts are charts *over the base field*, and the glued object is
    30	  covered by them as a `k`-scheme.
    31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` — being locally of finite type is local
    32	  on the source, so it descends from the charts to the glued object.
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_gluedHom` — over the affine base `Spec k`, quasi-compactness
    34	  of the glued object is compactness of its space, which a finite family of compact charts
    35	  supplies.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofCharts` — **the first producer of the Jacobian datum**:
    37	  a finite Zariski chart family of relatively representable open immersions into
    38	  `pic0SigmaSheaf C`, jointly locally surjective, with quasi-compact charts that are locally of
    39	  finite type over `k`, yields `JacobianData C`.
    40	
    41	## The hypothesis bundle
    42	
    43	Every declaration here carries exactly the three hypotheses of the frozen `Jacobian` of
    44	`Challenge.lean` — `IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  The
    45	`GeometricallyReduced C.hom` hypothesis of `Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` is *not* an extra assumption:
    46	a morphism smooth of relative dimension `1` is smooth (`Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`)
    47	and a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced (`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`), both global
    48	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, so instance resolution supplies it
    49	from the frozen bundle.  The `example` at the end of this file is the machine-checked record.
    50	-/
    51	
    52	set_option autoImplicit false
    53	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    54	
    55	universe u
    56	
    57	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    58	
    59	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    60	
    61	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    62	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    63	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    64	
    65	/-! ## Packaging a representation as the datum -/
    66	
    67	/-- **Package a representation of the degree-zero Picard functor**, with its two finiteness
    68	certificates, as the pinned Jacobian datum.  The representation is stated in the
    69	`pic0TypeFunctor` spelling; that abbreviation unfolds to the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage that
    70	`JacobianData.rep` is typed against. -/
    71	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    72	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    73	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
    74	    JacobianData C where
    75	  J := J
    76	  rep := rep
    77	  locallyOfFiniteType := hlft
    78	  quasiCompact := hqc
    79	
    80	@[simp]
    81	lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    82	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    83	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
    84	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).J = J :=
    85	  rfl
    86	
    87	@[simp]
    88	lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_rep (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    89	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    90	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
    91	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).rep = rep :=
    92	  rfl
    93	
    94	/-- The universal property of a packaged datum is the packaged representation. -/
    95	@[simp]
    96	lemma JacobianData.homEquiv_ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    97	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    98	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom)
    99	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (g : T ⟶ J) :
   100	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).homEquiv g = rep.homEquiv g :=
   101	  rfl
   102	
   103	/-! ## The chart family and its glued object -/
   104	
   105	section Charts
   106	
   107	variable {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   108	  (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   109	
   110	/-- **The structure morphism of the `i`-th chart** over the base field: the Σ-component of the
   111	element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.  A chart of the degree-zero Picard sheaf
   112	is by construction a scheme *together with* a map to `Spec k`, namely the base over which the
   113	line bundle it classifies lives; this is that map. -/
   114	noncomputable def chartHom (i : ι) : X i ⟶ Spec (.of k) := (yonedaEquiv (f i)).1
   115	
   116	variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
   117	variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
   118	
   119	/-- **The structure morphism of the glued object of a chart family**: mathlib's 01JJ engine
   120	glues the charts into a scheme representing the Σ-extension sheaf, and the Σ-component of the
   121	universal element of that representation is the map of that scheme to `Spec k`. -/
   122	noncomputable abbrev gluedHom :
   123	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
   124	  ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
   125	    (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1
   126	
   127	/-- **The glued object of a chart family**, as a scheme over the base field.  This is the
   128	object represented by `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`. -/
   129	noncomputable abbrev gluedOfCharts : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk (gluedHom C f hf)
   130	
   131	  exact HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›
   132	
   133	/-! ## The producer -/
   134	
   135	/-- **The first producer of the Jacobian datum**: a Zariski chart family of relatively
   136	representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf of the degree-zero Picard functor,
   137	jointly locally surjective, indexed by a finite type, with quasi-compact charts that are locally
   138	of finite type over the base field, produces the pinned representability datum of the curve.
   139	
   140	The representing object is the glued scheme of the family, placed over `Spec k` by the

===0d465e95d9===
0d465e95d99be0370e72af6ff6581eb7e2de534c
Archon Horizon <archon@archon-horizon.local>
feat(picrep): terminal-representability bridge for pointwise-unique presheaves
New Picard/RepresentableByTerminal.lean: `representableByTerminal` builds
`F.RepresentableBy Y` for any terminal `Y` from `Nonempty (F.obj T)` and
`Subsingleton (F.obj T)` at every test `T`, plus the `Unique`-packaged form and
an `IsRepresentable` corollary. This is the presheaf-side companion of mathlib's
`hasTerminal_of_unique`, absent from mathlib v4.31 (verified by search).

It is the interface that converts `DivFamilyZero.instNonemptyObjZero` (the empty
divisor, landed) plus the open `Subsingleton ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj T)` into
AJC's first genuine `RepresentableBy` producer, at the terminal `Over.mk (𝟙 S)`.
The `Subsingleton` is not discharged here; this file supplies only the reusable
categorical bridge it plugs into. All three declarations axiom-clean
[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; rooted at AlgebraicJacobian.lean.


===aa38db9d26===
aa38db9d26f288455d3ffcbbb2f788214281ddef
Archon Horizon <archon@archon-horizon.local>
feat(picrep): Div⁰ RepresentableBy producer modulo degree-0 divisor uniqueness
Two coherent pieces toward AJC's first genuine RepresentableBy producer on the
divisor side (AJC.picrep.divzero):

- RepresentableByTerminal.lean: generalise the terminal bridge to three
  universes (w v u) so it applies to the Type (u+1)-valued DivFunctorDeg; the
  earlier commit tied the value universe to the morphism universe and did not fit.

- DivFamilyZero.lean §5: `divFunctorDegZero_representableByTerminal` — Div⁰_{X/S}
  is RepresentableBy the terminal object Over.mk (𝟙 S), GIVEN that every degree-0
  relative effective divisor is the empty divisor (`hrel`). The Nonempty half is
  the landed empty divisor; `subsingleton_divFunctorDegZero_obj_of_forall_rel_zero`
  peels the Subtype/Quotient layer off the obligation, leaving the honest
  geometric statement `x.HasFiberDeg 0 → x.Rel (DivFamily.zero)`.

The antecedent `hrel` is the WHOLE of what remains, is non-circular (mentions no
RepresentableBy), and is not P → P. No hypothesis on π. Both new declarations
axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] against fgaPicardRepresentability
firing sorryAx in the same probe. lake build AlgebraicJacobian EXIT=0 (8617 jobs).

feat(picrep): sharpen Div⁰ producer obligation to coherent-sheaf vanishing

divisor family with zero structure sheaf is the empty divisor) and the sharper
producer `divFunctorDegZero_representableByTerminal_of_isZero`, whose single
antecedent is `x.HasFiberDeg 0 → IsZero x.F`: pure coherent-sheaf vanishing, no
divisor/quotient/Picard vocabulary. This is the honest remaining gap of

finrank-based fiberDeg makes the natural target). Both new declarations

feat(pic): IsZero-from-sections converse for sheaves of modules
Add isZero_of_forall_subsingleton_sections and the packaged
isZero_iff_forall_subsingleton_sections in DivFamilyZero.lean §2: a sheaf of
modules on a scheme is zero iff its sections vanish over every open. This is the
exact converse of the existing subsingleton_sections_of_isZero, mathlib-absent,
and the honest section-level target for 'a divisor family cuts out the empty
divisor' (the divzero row's remaining obligation). Reusable vanishing criterion
across the Picard files.

the sharpest reduction of the divzero producer, with the IsZero antecedent
